subject: general
question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the conduct of business of the Government of a state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 166**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 166 of the Constitution of India deals with the conduct of business of the Government of a state:
 
• All executive action of the state government must be taken in the name of the Governor.
 
• The Governor makes rules for the transaction of state government business and allocates it among ministers.
 
• Orders and instruments made in the name of the Governor are authenticated in a manner specified by the Governor's rules. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Article 164
 
 
• The Governor appoints the Chief Minister and other Ministers, who serve at the Governor's pleasure. 
 
• Ministers are responsible for the conduct of government business. 
 
 
 
• Article 167
 
 
• The Chief Minister is responsible for providing information to the Governor about the state's administration. 
 
 
 
• Article 177
 
 
• The rights of Ministers and the Advocate-General in relation to the Houses are defined
